correctness.rationale: Proposition 7.1 explicitly puts the four quadrangle generators a,b,c,d into acl(e,f,g) and exhibits a parameter-fixing involution moving them. Because those four generate pi^4 under definable join/meet terms, all of pi^4 lies in acl(e,f,g). Since pi^4 is elementary in the ambient model, algebraic closure over its parameters cannot acquire elements outside it. Hence acl(e,f,g)=pi^4, while dcl is proper.

value.rationale: The result sharpens a qualitative acl-versus-dcl example into an exact algebraic-closure computation: three geometric parameters algebraically generate an entire countably infinite elementary free plane. This makes the closure geometry of the stable theory substantially more concrete and connects the complete-quadrilateral configuration directly to an elementary submodel.
